He stayed on powerfully up the hill to prevail by a neck from Lulamba, making a stunning start over hurdles. He can only improve from that experience and is taken to confirm the form. Lulamba was making his fourth start over jumps at Cheltenham and did little wrong. He met some traffic after the second-last, but it didn't look to have any bearing on the result. Murcia was impressive when winning the Grade 1 at Aintree and that was an improved effort. She also has to enter calculations.

selections.comment: Connections have had to be patient with QUANTUM BOY, who appears for Willie Mullins now having been a very impressive point-to-point winner back in November 2023. The Diamond Boy gelding was snapped up by JP McManus after his 40-length win at Damma House and is a fascinating runner on his racecourse bow. English point-to-point winner Panjandrum makes his first start for Gordon Elliott and Gigginstown. He cost 95,000 pounds after scoring at Chaddesley Corbett in December. Lucinda Russell introduces an interesting newcomer in Biglesisback. The Walk In The Park mare carries the colours of Kenny Alexander and is a half-sister to his Cheltenham winner Doddiethegreat.

selections.comment: TAKE A BREATH looks to have been handed a gilt edged opportunity by the handicapper and is fancied to kick of his season in style and claim top spot. Form figures of 435 are a bit misleading consisdering he was beaten less than a length the last twice and only six lengths by Sandtrap (second in a French G2 next time) on debut. Native Honey was unfancied on season debut last time and a 6th of 8 looks pretty unininspiring but he was denied a clear run at a critical stage and his winning chance vanished. He may have gone close. Better is expected eased back in grade off a further 2lb drop. Patsy Snugfit is another to have endured a miserable time of it late on last time when squeezed out by the first two and slipping back to fifth. She wouldn't have been beaten far. A close-up third on her debut last term bodes well for her season bow today and she can make the frame

selections.comment: Danzart should prove popular in a bid to land a double dropped back to 6f after a narrow victory over 7f here last month. He's a three time winner over six furlongs so must be feared but 7f looks his optimum trip now and the combination of drop in trip and 4lb rise makes it tough and he's taken on. ONE MORE DREAM looks the solid option. He won a 5f event at Pontefract when returned to turf last month for the first time in a while exploiting his much lower turf mark and is back on turf off a 3lb higher mark having gone well switched to the AW last time. The step back up to 6f should be fine and the son of Bated Breath can score again. Captain Vello is in good spirits and back over his optimum trip can make the frame

selections.comment: This probably hinges on whether TRUST SERGEI can prove as effective back up in trip having opened his account when dropped back to a sharp 5f. There's no doubt stamina concerns, as he faded away on his first three career runs between 6f and 7f before a more promising 3rd on handicap debut in a 6f event. He flattened out that day but was beaten under two lengths and perhaps most of the improvement next time was down to natural progression not just the drop back to 5f. This is only his second turf run (poor on debut on soft ground) but he remains well-handicapped and can lead them home. Alashos looks best placed to expolit any frailties of the selection. James Horton's gelding flopped badly last time when favourite but it may pay to excuse that effort as he seemed to resent the first-time blinkers holding his head high and never travelled. Now with cheekpieces (worn three previous runs) replacing the offending blinkers he can get back on track. Rogue Dancer and Moby Quick are respected but Chuti Manika is next on the list having made a very encouraging season bow last time when narrowly touched off again (has been beaten less than a length last three runs now). Charlie Johnston's colt is dependable and shouldn't be far away

selections.comment: BAS BLEU has a good opportunity to gain his first win on turf having kicked off this term with a fine third beaten less than a length at Kempton following on form a win at the same venue on final run last term. Before that he proved at least as effective on turf and a bit of improvement can be reasonably expected on this second run of the season. He should prove tough to master. Melek Alreeh was in top form when last seen in November landing a class 5 handicap for a second win at Southwell. On balance his AW form is a bit better than on turf but he's less exposed on grass and his only other win came over CD on fast ground on second career start. He can go very well fresh and is greatly feared. Squeezbox has cliams back at his optimum trip but may struggle a bit upped in class so Isle Of Stark may prove more of a danger returned to Flat action having been campaigned over jumps this winter. The pick of his Flat form offers hope and off a career low mark he can make his presence felt

selections.comment: A weak race and a good opportunity for PRECIOUS SPARTAN to open his account. Nigel Tinkler's gelding was beaten under a length last time trying 1m2f for the first time and saw out the trip well. He lacked a touch of pace then but in this company has less to fear on that count. He should be in the shake-up. He split a pair of next time out winners when runner up on his last hurdles run and has proven himself versatile ground wise recently. A mark of 99 looks to underestimate his ability. Tees Comp's Clive failed to convince with his stamina last time but he is well treated on the best of his winter form and is a possible improver following a wind op. He can chase the selection home ahead of course winner Blame Rose who has dropped to an attractive mark but could do with some rain.

This longer trip could bring out significant improvement if he can get his jumping together. UK raider Herakles Westwood is also feared having run welll behind the future Irish National winner last time.

This included LULAMBA who also made mistakes at key stages and looked a slightly unlucky loser. He can make amends and reverse form with the horse who mugged him late. Of those in behind the pair Too Bossy For Us may do best at potentially big odds. He was never put into the race at Cheltenham but finished well under tender handling and is expected to come on for that experience.

selections.comment: Though HEY SUNSHINE lost her unbeaten hurdles record on her recent reappearance it came on unsuitably soft ground and she likely needed the outing. She can get back on track here off what looks a lenient opening mark on her Listed win. She was a comfortable winner that day and both placed horses behind her have won at the same level since. Grand Annual winner Jazzy Matty is feared most as he shaped very well off a much lower hurdles mark on ground softer than ideal last time and has won over this longer trip over fences. D Art D Art was well fancied for the Pertemps and ran well for a long way until his stamina gave way. Back down in trip he should be thereabouts at the finish.

selections.comment: This couple be fought out by a trio of point winners making their rules debuts. QUANTUM BOY appeals most despite the long absence as his win was by 40l and he represents the Mullins yard who have a fine record in this discipline. Panjandrum made amends for a fall when winning last time while Obey The Order was impressive in the spring. They are both respected and worth following in the betting.

selections.comment: JUNGLE COVE was well held in this last year but has been successful over hurdles and on the flat since so is fancied to make a winning reappearance on favourable drying ground. Dark Note was in decent form in this sphere in the autumn and can make his presence felt. Multiple hurdles and chase winner A Mere Bagatelle could fare best of the Shark Hanlon horses and gain a place.
